short: Appeasement's author: he returned from Munich promising peace for our time.
full:
Neville Chamberlain became prime minister in May 1937, aged sixty-eight, after a career as a reforming health minister and a competent chancellor. He believed personal diplomacy could contain Hitler and flew to Germany three times in September 1938. The Munich Agreement handed the Sudetenland to Germany without Czechoslovak consent; Chamberlain returned to Heston aerodrome waving a paper and told the crowd he believed it was peace for our time.

Germany occupied the rest of Czechoslovakia in March 1939, and Britain guaranteed Poland. Chamberlain declared war on 3 September 1939, having also overseen the rearmament - radar, Spitfires and Hurricanes - that made 1940 survivable. The failure of the Norwegian campaign brought a Commons debate in May 1940 in which his majority fell from over two hundred to eighty-one, and he resigned on 10 May, the day Germany invaded the Low Countries. He served under Churchill until cancer forced him out, and died that November.
